prompt:
Create a high-fidelity desktop web app UI comp at 1440x1000 for “Alloc”, a local financial intelligence operations dashboard. This is not a marketing page. Visual world: a surveyor’s field ledger on a daylight operations desk, translated into a modern interface with exceptional craft. Restrained light palette: mineral paper #F3F0E7, deep graphite #18201D, surveyor green #1F6A4A, safety vermilion #D34A32 only for errors, cobalt ink #2F55A4 for links/provenance, muted brass #B58B3A for pending. Use a precise humanist sans for UI and a compact serif only for major ledger totals; tabular numerals. No generic grid of floating cards, no gradients, no glass, no oversized hero metric.

Composition: a narrow dark graphite left rail with Alloc mark and five icon+text nav items (Overview, Requests, Memory, Forecast, Activity), plus a three-company switcher. The main canvas feels like an open field ledger: a strong header line reading “Northstar Fieldworks” and “Quarter in view · Synthetic mock data”, with a small mock API status. Under it, create an asymmetric first viewport. Left two-thirds: a canonical exposure ledger as one continuous ruled sheet showing Authorized $500.00, Recognized $120.00, Committed $180.00, Available $200.00 and a horizontal proportional allocation band. Overlay one translucent green acetate sheet partially across this ledger titled “Field Engineering · category view — do not add to total” with precise registration holes and source/version annotations. Right third: “Needs a human” review queue as a hinged ochre paper slip, featuring Maya Chen’s Buffalo pilot trip, revised total $240.00, +$60 cumulative, reason “Cumulative amendment limit exceeded,” and a clear “Review request” action. Beneath the ledger, show a slim activity register and a forecast horizon strip rather than cards. Include subtle punched reference marks and fine 1px rules, square-to-8px corners, real product copy, clear focus states, and prominent labels that data is synthetic/mock-backed. Avoid fintech clichés, rounded card grids, decorative charts, and excessive whitespace. The result should look like a production-ready financial operations tool, dense but calm, trustworthy, readable, and distinctive.
